name: Borommarachathirat I
contribution: The third king of the Ayutthaya Kingdom.

checks.lead: King Borommarachathirat I (Thai: สมเด็จพระบรมราชาธิราชที่ ๑, romanized: RTGS: Somdet Phra Borommarachathirat Thi Nueng), also known as Khunluang Pha Ngua (Thai: ขุนหลวงพะงั่ว; "King Pha Ngua"; r. 1370–1388), was the third king of the Ayutthaya Kingdom. He was the elder brother of King Ramathibodi I's consort, and so his brother-in-law, and the maternal uncle of King Ramesuan. Before taking the throne at Ayutthaya he ruled Suphan Buri under Ramathibodi I. Less than a year after King Uthong's death, he forced King Ramesuan from power and seized the throne. After his death in 1388, his son Thong Lan reigned for only a week before Ramesuan, who had retreated to Lavo, returned and overthrew him. Ramesuan later reclaimed the throne for a second reign.
